I am leaning towards setting more writing goals. I want to continue with coding, and in an effort to prerase regrets, I want to give writing a Real Try. When I think of what I would do if I didn't need to earn money, writing is consistently in my top ten, in fact it is something I do nearly daily even without the pay. It occurred to me the other day that if I could get paid a Living Wage for it, I could commit to writing for a full-time work-week. For the record, that ought to be about 30 hours, but I think I could do 35-40 happily, if it meant basic financial security. Wise people would recommend pursuing endeavors one feels this way about, but I don't even know what kind of writer I am-I don't think I'm a novelist, but I may be an essayist. Or a speechwriter? Then again maybe I'm not good enough at either of those to convince someone else to pay me for it. I admit I have not given any of it a wholehearted try. I do write a lot of diary entries. Also diatribes and rants. Who wants to hire me to rant??

Does coding include enough writing to satisfy a Real Try? Is engineering software my best path? I started off wanting to freelance, but maybe I'd garner more security as an employee. I know experienced programmers consistently advise it's never too late to learn, and there are still Good Jobs for Good Learners, plus I feel confident in soft skills that I keep hearing are more in demand since those are harder to train people in. However, doubts remain. I know Doubt can't ever be eradicated. And I'd have at least as much doubt in sidelining coding and investing all my time in writing. I wish I had a mentor, guru, or trustworthy parent to tell me what I'm meant to do. Add it to the list of wasteful wishes.

I predict it's reasonable to write for at least 25 minutes/one typed or handwritten page per day. And work on programming at least 25 minutes per day/about 3 hours per week. Networking in either arena counts. Bonus points if I publish my writing to Medium or Substack.
